title: Oral candidiasis (thrush) in an asthmatic: nystatin
vignette: A 6-year-old asthmatic has the finding shown in the image on routine examination: thick, white, curd-like plaques on the tongue and buccal mucosa that can be scraped off. The child uses an inhaled corticosteroid for asthma control. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for the lesions on this patient's oral mucosa?

clues.note: Inhaled corticosteroids (used for asthma) predispose to oral candidiasis (thrush) by local immunosuppression.

clues.text: thick, white, curd-like plaques on the tongue and buccal mucosa that can be scraped off
clues.note: White plaques that scrape off (leaving an erythematous base) are oral thrush - localized Candida (oropharyngeal candidiasis).

whatMatters: White, scrapeable oral plaques in a child on inhaled corticosteroids = ORAL CANDIDIASIS (thrush). In an immunocompetent patient, localized thrush is treated with a TOPICAL antifungal - NYSTATIN (a polyene, 'swish and swallow'), which is not absorbed from the GI tract. Answer D.
strategy: Diagnose thrush (Candida) and pick a TOPICAL antifungal for localized disease in an immunocompetent child: nystatin (or clotrimazole troches). Reject acyclovir (antiviral - HSV), amphotericin B (IV polyene for systemic mycoses, too toxic for thrush), griseofulvin and terbinafine (for dermatophytes, not Candida), and penicillin (antibacterial - no antifungal activity).

eliminations.label: Acyclovir - antiviral (HSV/VZV)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a nucleoside analog antiviral for herpes simplex and varicella-zoster. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: thrush is FUNGAL (Candida), not viral; acyclovir has no antifungal activity. ✅ Correct if: herpetic oral ulcers/gingivostomatitis.

eliminations.label: Amphotericin B - IV, reserved for systemic mycoses
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a polyene antifungal (like nystatin) used INTRAVENOUSLY for serious systemic fungal infections. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is too toxic for a simple mucocutaneous infection; localized thrush is treated topically. ✅ Correct if: invasive/systemic mycosis in an immunocompromised host.

eliminations.label: Griseofulvin - dermatophytes only
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an antifungal that disrupts fungal mitosis, used for DERMATOPHYTE infections (tinea). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is not effective against Candida. ✅ Correct if: dermatophytosis (e.g., tinea capitis).

eliminations.label: Penicillin - antibacterial
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a beta-lactam ANTIBACTERIAL that inhibits peptidoglycan cross-linking. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it has no antifungal activity (and antibiotics can even predispose to candidiasis). ✅ Correct if: a susceptible bacterial infection.

eliminations.label: Terbinafine - dermatophytes (onychomycosis)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an allylamine antifungal concentrating in skin/nails, used for dermatophytosis/onychomycosis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is not the treatment for oral candidiasis. ✅ Correct if: nail/skin dermatophyte infection.

reasoning: White, scrapeable oral plaques in a child on inhaled corticosteroids = oral candidiasis (thrush)
Localized thrush in an immunocompetent patient is treated with a topical antifungal
Nystatin is a topical polyene antifungal ('swish and swallow'), not absorbed from the GI tract
mechanism: Oral thrush (oropharyngeal candidiasis) is a localized Candida infection producing thick white plaques on the tongue/buccal mucosa that scrape off to leave an erythematous base. It is common with local or systemic immunosuppression - here from INHALED CORTICOSTEROIDS (asthma), which locally blunt mucosal defenses (rinsing the mouth after inhaler use reduces risk). In IMMUNOCOMPETENT patients, localized candidiasis is treated with a TOPICAL antifungal. NYSTATIN is a POLYENE antifungal (mechanism like amphotericin B) that binds ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane, forming pores that leak intracellular contents; it is NOT absorbed from the GI tract, so it is given as an oral 'swish and swallow' suspension acting locally on the mucosa (clotrimazole troches are an alternative). It is the drug of choice for oropharyngeal candidiasis without advanced immunodeficiency (severe/systemic disease warrants systemic azoles like fluconazole). The distractors treat other pathogens: acyclovir (viral), amphotericin B (systemic fungal, IV/toxic), griseofulvin and terbinafine (dermatophytes), and penicillin (bacterial).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro/Pharm > oral candidiasis: risk with inhaled steroids/immunosuppression; treat localized disease with topical nystatin (polyene, binds ergosterol, 'swish and swallow'); systemic azole if severe.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: White scrapeable plaques + inhaled steroids = thrush -> topical nystatin.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on oral candidiasis/thrush, polyene antifungal, ergosterol, or 'swish and swallow'? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Acyclovir (viral), amphotericin B (systemic/toxic), griseofulvin/terbinafine (dermatophytes), penicillin (bacterial) don't treat localized thrush.

difficulty.text: On the photo: creamy white plaques coat the tongue/buccal mucosa (would scrape off leaving a red base) - oral thrush. Anchor: 'white scrapeable oral plaques = Candida = nystatin.'
